questions.question: If you are turning left and there are two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: Trucks should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to make left turns. Use the right turn lane to begin your turn.

questions.question: What is a danger of a large truck swerving to avoid a hazard?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.
Other vehicles may do the same thing.

questions.explanation: Swerving can be safer than stopping suddenly. However, heavy or top-heavy trucks pulling trailers can roll over when swerving.

questions.question: After a crash, which action should you NOT take?
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, call authorities, and help injured people. Never leave the scene.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you fall behind on sleep
When you want to take a nap
The amount of time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you fall behind on sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not get enough sleep. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: When inspecting a double or triple trailer, what should you do?

options.text: To save time, not all parts need to be inspected.
A driver should only inspect the first trailer and its parts.
A driver should only inspect the rear trailer and its parts.
A driver should inspect all parts to ensure safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should inspect all parts to ensure safety.
questions.explanation: Inspect double and triple trailers the same way you inspect other vehicles. Check all parts, even though it takes more time.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents.
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, keep cargo low and centered. Turn slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single vehicles. They require more skill to drive safely.

questions.question: How can you tell if a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working when you start the engine?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
The red light on the trailer will flash three times and then stay on.
All the rear lights on the trailer will flash and then shut off.
The blue light near the driver's door will light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with ABS have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after starting the engine, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a long trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness, get enough sleep before the trip, plan your route and stops ahead of time, drive with a passenger, and drive during hours when you are normally awake.

questions.question: What should you do if fog covers the road?
questions.explanation: Fog makes driving dangerous. Avoid driving in fog when possible.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: When using controlled braking in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Push the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Use about half your normal braking force.
Push the brakes so the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pushing the brakes hard without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small when braking this way.

questions.question: When you check coupling equipment before driving, the fifth wheel should be:
questions.explanation: Check that all coupling parts are present and working. The fifth wheel should be properly greased and securely mounted.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to remove the vehicle.
Walk on the tracks to look for a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Call emergency services.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand to keep the other free.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.
At the bottom of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: What should you do when facing an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: Get out of the way if possible. Do not challenge the driver, make eye contact, or react to rude gestures.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles can enter.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is there.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. Other drivers will have time to react if you missed seeing them.

questions.question: What danger can happen if your vehicle rolls backward when starting?

options.text: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
You may lose your spot in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a stop. If you have a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: Keep all shut-off valves open except the last valves on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all brakes and prevents air from escaping the back of the vehicle.
